propositions: The test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer test intermittently kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 because it executes ~1768 serial pandoc spawns across 884 renderable units in a single monolithic loop, taking 91.6s idle and 504.8s under CPU saturation—1.7x past CI's 300s per-test timeout guard.

pytest-timeout with --timeout-method=thread calls os._exit(1) from its timer thread when the budget is exceeded, killing the worker process outright with no traceback or assertion text rather than failing the test cleanly.
The test cost is unbounded and load-dependent; macOS runner contention is routine, making only that cell red while identical commits pass on other platforms.

The fix replaces the monolithic loop with chunk-parametrized tests using a fixed _EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK=40 constant, ensuring per-test cost is bounded by construction regardless of corpus growth and allowing xdist to spread work across workers.

A new coverage guard test (test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit) verifies that all chunks reassemble to exactly _renderable_units() and that >= 100 units are covered, preventing silent unit drops.
All 884 units remain compared against the oracle with real pandoc at stride 1; the byte-identity property is untouched and no timeout raise, retry marker, or elapsed-time assertion is added.
